rfi.title: Tiny French outpost off Canada the unlikely stage for new transatlantic courtship
rfi.description: A tiny piece of France just off Canada’s Atlantic coast will become the setting for a much bigger geopolitical story on Sunday, when President Emmanuel Macron welcomes Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to Saint-Pierre and Miquelon. The meeting brings Canada’s push for closer ties with Europe to a territory that has long sat at the crossroads of French, Canadian and US interests in the North Atlantic.

rfi.title: Sweeping raids leave Turkey’s LGBTQI+ community fearing what comes next
rfi.description: Turkey has jailed dozens of people pending trial as a sweeping crackdown on LGBTQI+ groups widens, prompting international condemnation and protests outside Turkish embassies on Friday.

rfi.title: Russians vote for new parliament after campaign marked by near silence
rfi.description: Russians began voting on Friday in three days of parliamentary elections to choose the 450 members of the State Duma, after a campaign with little public debate or television coverage. More than four years into the war in Ukraine, candidates have also had few opportunities to challenge Kremlin policies.

rfi.title: Locked in Arctic ice, the floating lab studying climate and wildlife
rfi.description: A floating laboratory has begun drifting through Arctic sea ice on a mission set to last until late 2027, carrying scientists into one of the most isolated places on Earth. Built in France, the Tara Polar Station is carrying a crew of 12 to study biodiversity and the effects of climate change, as well as a dog to alert them to polar bears – and no one knows exactly where the ice will take them.

rfi.title: French police officer detained over terror plot linked to far-right ideology

rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened a criminal investigation into suspected sexual harassment involving smart glasses, after complaints about women being filmed in the street without their knowledge and the footage being posted online.

rfi.title: Algeria shifts towards English as French loses ground in schools
rfi.description: Primary school pupils in Algeria are in for a change this year when, for the first time, the national curriculum will focus on English over French. The move follows a general trend across former French colonies in North Africa that are now prioritising English.

rfi.title: Nestlé to face retrial over illegal dumping near French bottled water plants
rfi.description: Nestlé Waters is to face a new trial over alleged illegal dumping near its bottled water plants in eastern France, after an appeals court reinstated key scientific evidence excluded from the original proceedings.

rfi.title: A city at the crossroads of history: Unearthing Gaza's ancient heritage
rfi.description: Before Gaza became synonymous with conflict, it was a place where merchants sold wine from local vineyards, pilgrims crossed continents, fishermen set out before dawn, and generations of families lived between sea and desert. RFI explores its deep history.

rfi.title: Canada and EU 'stronger together' says Carney, brushing aside US threats
rfi.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday welcomed a proposal for his country to become the European Union's first "associate member", shrugging off threats from United States President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: From Peru to the Philippines, defending the land comes at a deadly cost
rfi.description: People defending their land, forests and communities continue to face killings, arrests and intimidation around the world – with Latin America by far the most dangerous region, the environmental campaign group Global Witness has found. In the Philippines, one community resisting a mining project has told RFI of arrests, injuries and legal action against residents trying to stop work on their land.

rfi.title: Dry rivers and shrinking glaciers deepen global freshwater decline
rfi.description: Rivers around the world are running unusually dry as freshwater reserves continue to decline, leaving less water stored away to help countries through drought, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned. Glaciers and groundwater are also shrinking, while in Switzerland the retreat of Alpine ice is already forcing changes to infrastructure that supplies hydroelectric power.

rfi.title: French fishermen renew protest as France boosts aid over soaring fuel prices
rfi.description: French fishermen renewed protests over rising fuel costs on Thursday despite the government increasing subsidies for the sector and extending support for farmers and construction companies. Diesel prices are nearing a record high, fuelling wider concern over the cost of living and calls for protests reminiscent of the Yellow Vest movement, seven months before the presidential election.

USA: Pistorius nimmt in Texas ersten F-35-Kampfjet für Deutschland entgegen
zeit.description: Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius hat im US-Bundesstaat Texas den ersten Kampfjet vom Typ F-35 entgegengenommen. Insgesamt acht Flugzeuge werden geliefert.

zeit.title: Nach Einigung: Schnieder: Entlastungen bei Spritpreisen «wichtiges Signal»
Tankpreis: Regierung einigt sich auf Tankrabatt und Spritpreisdeckel
zeit.description: Die Koalition hat einen neuen Tankrabatt und einen Spritpreisdeckel beschlossen. Die Preise für Sprit sollen ab dem 1. Oktober um 17 Cent pro Liter gesenkt werden.

zeit.title: Zum siebten Mal 2026: Stromnetz auf Kuba bricht erneut zusammen
Landtagswahl in MV: MV-Wahlkampfendspurt: AfD und SPD in Umfrage Kopf an Kopf
Entlastungen: Tankrabatt und Preisdeckel - Was bringen die Maßnahmen?
Regulierung von künstlicher Intelligenz: Wie sich KI sicherer machen lässt
zeit.description: Die Chefs der wichtigsten KI-Unternehmen warnen vor einer Katastrophe und fordern mehr Überwachung. Braucht es eine Atombehörde für KI?

zeit.title: Parteiensystem in Italien: Das Land, das seine Populisten überlebte
zeit.description: Italien ist es gelungen, in 35 Jahren mehrere Wellen des Populismus zu überstehen. Diese Erfahrung zeigt Deutschland, wie widerstandsfähig eine Demokratie sein kann.

zeit.title: Roger G.: »Entweder es knallt, oder sie trinken Bier zusammen«
zeit.description: Eigentlich scherzt der Comedian Roger G. über Möwen und Gurken. Vor der Wahl in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern kritisiert er die AfD, deren Wähler auch in seinem Publikum sitzen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: Trump entzieht CNN und «Politico» Zugang zum Weissen Haus
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Hat sich Granit Xhaka, der Captain des Fussball-Nationalteams, ein gefälschtes Covid-Zertifikat besorgt?
nzz.description: Die Causa taugt zum Skandal, Ausgang offen. Klar ist: Die Staatsanwaltschaft Luzern ermittelt gegen Granit Xhaka und eine Ärztin.

nzz.title: «Aus Sicht des Bundesrates höchst problematisch»: Beat Jans muss wieder eine SVP-Initiative bekämpfen, dieses Mal ist es die Grenzschutzinitiative
nzz.description: Die SVP will die Grenzen systematisch kontrollieren lassen. Damit setze man Schengen-Dublin aufs Spiel, sagt der Bundesrat.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Volkswagen erwartet für 2026 tiefen Gewinn +++ Bank of Japan erhöht Leitzins auf höchsten Stand seit 31 Jahren
Wie tropische Mücken in Deutschland Flughafenmalaria verbreiten
nzz.description: In Frankfurt am Main haben per Flugzeug eingeschleppte Mücken sechs Mitarbeiter des Flughafens mit Malaria infiziert, diese Woche kamen noch zwei Anwohner hinzu. Drei der Erkrankten sind an der Tropenkrankheit verstorben.

nzz.title: Messerattacke von Oerlikon: «Besonders verwerflich war die Motivation» – chinesischer Student wegen mehrfachen versuchten Mordes schuldig gesprochen
nzz.description: Am Freitag ist der Mann, der 2024 Kindergartenkinder mit einem Messer angriff, zu fünfzehn Jahren Freiheitsstrafe verurteilt worden. Ein Brief ermöglicht Einblicke in das Leben der Opfer.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Polizei-News aus Zürich: Rauch quillt aus dem bekanntesten Fotomuseum der Schweiz
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

nzz.title: Glencore suspendiert Mitarbeiter, der die Deals mit dem kontroversen Händler Radiant betreute
nzz.description: Der internationale Handel mit Eisenerz ist ein Milliardengeschäft. Mehrere Schweizer Finanz- und Handelshäuser sind von der mutmasslichen Betrugsaffäre betroffen.

nzz.title: Braun statt bunt: Die Hitze lässt die Herbstfarben des Waldes verblassen
nzz.description: So heiss wie im Hitzesommer 2026 war es noch nie. Mit den Extremtemperaturen und der Trockenheit stehen die Bäume unter Dauerstress. Für Buchen und Fichten gibt der Boden nicht mehr genug Wasser her.

nzz.title: Putin stellt Nestlés Russland-Geschäft unter Zwangsverwaltung – Bundesbern zeigt sich besorgt
nzz.description: Der Kreml geht gegen westliche Firmen vor, die in Russland geblieben sind. Die Schweiz zähle zu den «unfreundlichen» Ländern, lautet die Begründung. Nestlé droht die Enteignung.

nzz.title: Neue Dimension des Wirtschaftskriegs: Russland greift ukrainische Übergänge an der Westgrenze an
nzz.description: Die Verbindungsrouten nach Westen sind Lebensadern für die Ukraine. Seit einigen Wochen versucht Russland diese zu kappen.

nzz.title: Kylian Mbappé kooperiert mit On: Die Schweizer Firma will mit dem Superstar den umkämpften Fussballmarkt erobern
nzz.description: Der Sportartikelhersteller wagt sich in neue Gefilde vor. Neben Mbappé ist mit seinem Landsmann Thierry Henry ein weiterer grosser Name an Bord.

nzz.title: Der Auftrag lautet «eliminieren» – die USA legen eine russische Geheimdienstzelle lahm
nzz.description: Fünf Männer sollen im Auftrag russischer Geheimdienste Attentate auf Kreml-Kritiker vorbereitet und Sabotageakte in Europa organisiert haben. Die amerikanische Justiz hat das mörderische Quintett nun angeklagt.

nzz.title: Mario Fehr sieht eine Chance für sich und tritt erneut an. Ganz ohne Partei im Rücken – warum auch, wenn man keine braucht?
nzz.description: Die Popularität des Zürcher Regierungsrats ist seit seinem Austritt aus der SP noch gestiegen. Weil er sich konsequent an sein eigenes Erfolgsrezept hält.

nzz.title: Nach der Entwendung von Kundendaten fordern Erpresser von Revolut 3 Millionen Dollar
nzz.description: Die Betrüger gelangten an die persönlichen Informationen der Neobank, indem sie sich als italienische Strafverfolgungsbehörde ausgaben. Unter den Opfern sind auch viele Schweizer.

nzz.title: Mindestens drei Tote bei einem Schusswaffenangriff an Schule auf den Philippinen
nzz.description: Auch der Angreifer ist offenbar unter den Toten. Laut den Behörden sind mehrere weitere Schüler zum Teil schwer verletzt worden.

france24fr.title: Robert Malley: "le processus d'Oslo était une illusion car fondé sur un malentendu historique"
france24fr.description: Robert Malley, chercheur  l'Université de Yale, est l'ancien conseiller de Bill Clinton, de Barack Obama et de Joe Biden sur le Moyen-Orient. Négociateur clé de l'accord sur le nucléaire iranien, il a aussi participé à des phases cruciales du processus de paix au Proche-Orient. Dans son livre "Demain c'est hier"  co-écrit avec Hussein Agha (éditions Max Milo), il livre ses réflexions sur 30 ans d'échec du processus de paix et imagine comment repenser la paix dans la région.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : Patrick Vieira dévoile sa première liste à la tête des Lions de la Teranga
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Patrick Vieira a dévoilé sa première liste avec le Sénégal pour les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Sadio Mané, absent pour un pépin physique, n’en fait pas partie. Le sélectionneur convoque 29 joueurs, avec les cadres et de nouveaux appelés dont Malang Sarr.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Donald Trump annonce interdire l'accès de la Maison Blanche à CNN, Politico et MSNOW
"Avec effet immédiat" : Trump annonce bannir CNN et deux autres médias de la Maison blanche
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi qu'il interdisait l'accès à la Maison Blanche aux médias CNN, MSNOW et Politico. Il les accusent, sans donner de détails, de diffuser "des fictions et des mensonges".

france24fr.title: Yémen, guerre "hybride" de la Russie et dangers de l'IA
france24fr.description: Au sommaire cette semaine : la guerre au Moyen-Orient et le front yéménite qui continue de s'embraser, les attaques hybrides menées par la Russie contre les pays européens et le débat autour des dangers de l'IA, qui pourrait anéantir l'Humanité selon certains lanceurs d'alerte.

france24fr.title: Côte d’Ivoire : « Pourquoi je ne pardonnerais pas à la France ? » Simone Ehivet
france24fr.description: Dans un entretien accordé à France 24, Simone Ehivet, en France pour la première fois depuis 2011, assure avoir pardonné à la France comme à Alassane Ouattara. L'ex-Première dame ivoirienne regrette, en outre, l'arrestation de proches de Laurent Gbagbo, parlant de "prisonniers politiques".

france24fr.title: L'UEFA et la Concacaf réclament à la Fifa "10 millions de dollars" pour chaque fédération
france24fr.description: Les présidents de l'UEFA et la Concacaf ont demandé, vendredi, au président de la Fifa, Gianni Infantino, de verser "au moins 10 millions de dollars" à chacune des 211 associations membres. Une somme qu'ils justifient par les réserves d'environ six milliards de dollars détenues par la fédération internationale.

france24fr.title: Les effets du phénomène El Nino se font ressentir jusqu'aux Antilles
france24fr.description: La Martinique subit une nouvelle vague de chaleur. Des températures records ont été enregistrées ces dernières semaines. La faute, notamment, au phénomène El Nino, particulièrement intense cette année.

france24fr.title: REPLAY - Zidane dévoile sa première liste en tant que sélectionneur de l'équipe de France
france24fr.description: Zinédine Zidane a rendu sa première copie ce vendredi 18 septembre à 18 h 00. Le nouveau sélectionneur des Bleus a annoncé sa liste de 23 joueurs sans le milieu Aurélien Tchouaméni ni l'attaquant Marcus Thuram, mais avec cinq nouveaux. L'ex numéro dix des Bleus annonce que Kylian Mbappé restera son capitaine dans la nouvelle composition, bien qu'il ne souhaite pas se prononcer sur ses pronostics concernant le Ballon d'or.

france24fr.title: Marie-Antoinette, de reine mal-aimée à première influenceuse de France
france24fr.description: Plus de deux cents ans après son exécution, Marie-Antoinette continue de fasciner. De Versailles à Fontainebleau, les hommages se multiplient. Au XVIIIe siècle déjà, la reine imposait ses codes vestimentaires et cultivait une image qui faisait parler d’elle dans toute l’Europe. Et si Marie-Antoinette était, finalement, la première influenceuse française ?

france24fr.title: Psychose du post-partum : donner la vie et perdre la raison
france24fr.description: Le procès de Lindsay Clancy a relancé aux États-Unis le débat sur la psychose du post-partum. Accusée d’avoir tué ses trois enfants, avant de tenter de se suicider, cette mère affirme avoir agi lors d’un épisode délirant. Comment reconnaître cette maladie psychiatrique rare et grave ? Quels sont ses symptômes et peut-on en guérir ?

france24fr.title: Bo French, ou quand les outrances Maga risquent de remettre les clés du pétrole texan aux démocrates
france24fr.description: Les outrances racistes de Bo French, candidat républicain à la direction de la commission ferroviaire du Texas, ont fait de cette obscure élection un phénomène médiatique national de la campagne des midterms. Il en va à la fois de la crédibilité électorale du mouvement Maga et de qui va diriger l’une des commissions les plus influentes aux États-Unis. Elle supervise en effet la régulation de tout le pétrole et le gaz du Texas.

france24fr.title: Tchad : la « Chad Jazz Education Academy » ouvre ses portes à Ndjamena
france24fr.description: Une école de musique jazz a ouvert ses portes à N'Djaména. Une première au Tchad. La Chad Jazz Education Academy lance donc officiellement la première formation musicale du pays. Des jeunes sélectionnés selon leurs aptitudes, suivront un cursus sous licence et recevront une formation spécialisée en jazz.

france24fr.title: Alerte sur l'intelligence artificielle américaine : quelle gouvernance pour l'IA ?
france24fr.description: L'intelligence artificielle est-elle en train de nous échapper ? Après plusieurs sorties de route, les géants de l'IA appellent à freiner son développement. Engagés dans la course, les PDG d'Anthropic, d'OpenAI et de X semblent s'accorder sur la nécessité de ralentir pour éviter le pire. Leur crainte est-elle fondée ? Soucieux de ne pas se laisser distancer par leurs concurrents, les industriels ont-ils vraiment peur de leur création ? En pleine compétition entre la Chine et les États-Unis, quel

france24fr.title: Anne-Sophie Pic : la cuisine est-elle un art ?
france24fr.description: "À l'Affiche" a rencontré Anne-Sophie Pic à l’occasion de l’ouverture de son nouveau restaurant parisien, installé au sein de la Fondation Cartier pour l’art contemporain. La cheffe française, la plus étoilée au monde, nous ouvre les portes de ce nouveau projet et dévoile les coulisses de la création de l’un de ses plats signature : les berlingots, réinventés dans une nouvelle déclinaison inspirée de la pyramide du Louvre.

france24fr.title: Hadja Lahbib : "Nous ne sommes ni en situation de paix, ni en situation de guerre"
france24fr.description: Cette semaine, Caroline De Camaret reçoit Hadja Lahbib, commissaire européenne à l'Égalité, état de préparation et gestion des crises. Elle tire les leçons d'un été de feux inédit, alerte sur les menaces hybrides et défend le projet européen face à la poussée des extrêmes.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : le Kennedy Center en passe d’être démoli ?
france24fr.description: Des photographies de l'AFP qui montrent Donald Trump en train de regarder un panneau semblant évoquer une démolition du Kennedy Center, haut lieu culturel de Washington que le président américain menace de condamner si son nom n'y est pas accolé, font jeudi le tour des médias.

france24fr.title: Discours sur l'État de l'Union : des annonces convaincantes ?
france24fr.description: Tous les yeux et les oreilles étaient tournés vers le Parlement européen de Strasbourg ce mercredi 16 septembre à l'occasion du traditionnel discours sur l'État de l'Union de la présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen. Un discours fleuve – le sixième du genre – sur les grandes orientations de sa politique européenne pour l'année à venir.

observador.title: CNN, MS NOW e Politico banidos da Casa Branca por Trump
observador.description: O Presidente dos EUA afirmou que a decisão tem efeitos imediatos, deixando ainda o aviso de que outros meios de comunicação podem ser sujeitos à mesma proibição.

observador.title: IA: relatório falso quase levou a confronto entre EUA e Chin
observador.description: Na primavera de 2026, um analista usou um chatbot para compilar informações militares. O resultado foi um relatório falso que levou os EUA a mobilizar forças para intercetar um navio chinês.

observador.title: A queda da AD nas sondagens ameaça o futuro do Governo?
observador.description: A descida para terceiro lugar expõe a erosão do apoio eleitoral. Ao focar-se nos pensionistas, o Governo arrisca alienar a classe trabalhadora e entregar os jovens aos partidos radicais.

observador.title: As notícias das 20h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: 19h. Chega entrega novo requerimento para CPI a Luís Neves
observador.description: André Ventura espera que o Presidente da Assembleia da República não coloque mais "obstáculos". Ainda neste jornal, subida das temperaturas para os próximos dias pode provocar onda de calor.

observador.title: IGAS quer pagamento à entrada do hospital para evitar dívida
observador.description: IGAS fez várias recomendações aos hospitais e à Administração Central do Sistema de Saúde sobre o acesso de não residentes ao SNS. Entidade quer também que as dívidas sejam tornadas públicas.

observador.title: Detido casal em Elvas "fortemente indiciado" de rapto
observador.description: A detenções ocorreram na quarta-feira. De acordo com a investigação da PSP, o casal dedicava-se ao empréstimo de dinheiro a diversas vítimas, procedendo depois à cobrança coerciva das dívidas.

observador.title: "Eu sou uma árvore!", terá dito Carlos no funeral de Diana
observador.description: O irmão da princesa relata no seu livro as reações dos membros da família real britânica no funeral de Diana, destacando a "falta de cuidado" do clã com Harry e a frieza de Carlos diante da ex-mulher.

observador.title: "O Hamas disse que ia desarmar. Testem-nos"
observador.description: MNE da Palestina acusa Israel de estar a aplicar o mesmo método que usou em Gaza à Cisjordânia. Eleições de novembro estão marcadas, mas AP abre a porta à suspensão. Entrevista a Varsen Aghabekian.

observador.title: Licença Parental. Parlamento volta a adiar votação
observador.description: É a segunda vez em dois dias que os deputados atiram a votação das mudanças na licença parental para a frente no calendário. Mas ainda querem resolver tema antes da discussão do OE.

observador.title: Carta aberta a PM diz que cuidadores são esquecidos
observador.description: "Cuidar de alguém dependente não é uma escolha de horário laboral. É um trabalho invisível de 24 horas por dia", escreveram quatro mães numa carta aberta endereçada ao primeiro-ministro.

observador.title: IPMA: " O fim de semana terá subida gradual de temperaturas"
observador.description: O fim de semana traz uma subida gradual das temperaturas em Portugal. Pode dar origem a uma onda de calor com valores muito acima da média, segundo Maria João Frada, do IPMA.

observador.title: MAI espera ter mais polícias em Lisboa até ao fim do ano
observador.description: Luís Neves afirmou que 2026 tem sido "um ano feliz" para a Polícia de Segurança Pública. "Há muitos anos que nenhum Governo autorizava que a polícia tivesse dois concursos" para recrutamento.

observador.title: ULS São José confirma saída de quatro anestesiologistas
observador.description: Unidade Local de Saúde São José confirma quatro rescisões no Hospital Dona Estefânia e alega que três já se encontravam ausentes há vários meses. O quarto exercia funções em tempo parcial.

observador.title: IA: o novo fim do mundo depois dos anteriores
observador.description: Alberto Gonçalves comenta os eventuais alarmismos no debate em redor da Inteligência Artificial

observador.title: Redução dos preços dos combustíveis? Partidos em desacordo
observador.description: Carlos Pereira (PS) defende a descida imediata do ISP e João Graça (CH)  exige um apoio urgente às famílias. Hugo Carneiro (PSD) diz que as medidas do Governo garantem um alívio real nas carteiras.

observador.title: Anthropic cria laboratório para investigação de medicamentos
observador.description: De forma discreta, o laboratório de IA instalou um laboratório em São Francisco para fazer experiências físicas e tentar acelerar a investigação de tratamentos para doenças raras.

observador.title: 18h. Combustíveis podem atingir preços mais altos de sempre
observador.description: É o que avança a ANAREC sobre a próxima semana. Ainda, auto-estrada do norte continua cortada a esta hora nos dois sentidos por causa de um incêndio na região de Aveiro.

spiegel.title: USA: Trump will CNN, »Politico« und MS Now aus Weißem Haus verbannen
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hat angekündigt zwei Fernsehsender und ein Nachrichtenportal den Zutritt zum Weißen Haus zu verweigern. Der Grund: angebliche »Fake News«.

spiegel.title: Stimmung in Deutschland: »Ob ich die wähle oder die – es ändert sich nichts« - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Der Wahlsieg der AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt erschüttert nicht nur das politische Berlin. Doch was sagen die Menschen genau?

spiegel.title: Spritpreise: Bundesregierung einigt sich auf Tankrabatt und Preisdeckel
spiegel.description: Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen haben sich die Koalition und die Bundesländer auf ein Spritpreis-Entlastungspaket verständigt. Unter anderem sollen Benzin und Diesel um 17 Cent je Liter günstiger werden.

spiegel.title: USA: Trump kippt CO₂-Regeln und befeuert Boom schmutziger KI-Gaskraftwerke
spiegel.description: Der Chef der US-Umweltschutzbehörde EPA will mit der Kontrolle von Schadstoffen aus Gas- und Kohlekraftwerken nichts mehr zu tun haben. Schon jetzt gelten fast keine Grenzwerte mehr. Das fördert den Bau umstrittener KI-Rechenzentren.

spiegel.title: Volkswagen kappt Gewinnerwartung für 2026 – Aktie rauscht ab
spiegel.description: Ein Prozent Umsatzrendite statt, wie bisher erwartet, vier bis fünfeinhalb Prozent: Volkswagen hat seine Gewinnprognose für das laufende Geschäftsjahr deutlich nach unten korrigiert. Die Kurse von VW und Porsche fielen daraufhin stark.

spiegel.title: Rente mit 63 ist besonders in Ostdeutschland ein Reizthema – zu Recht?
spiegel.description: Manuela Schwesig führt ihren fulminanten Wahlkampf auch gegen das Ende der abschlagsfreien Frührente: Das träfe den Osten besonders hart, sagt sie. Doch die Fakten sind längst nicht so eindeutig.

spiegel.title: Andrej Swjaginzew: Kreml stuft Oscar-nominierten Filmemacher als ausländischen Agenten ein
spiegel.description: Bei den Filmfestspielen in Cannes hat er Wladimir Putin aufgefordert, den Krieg in der Ukraine zu beenden. Nun hat Russland den Regisseur Andrej Swjaginzew zum ausländischen Agenten erklärt.

spiegel.title: Nigeria: Dutzende Bergleute ersticken offenbar in Gewahrsam von Paramilitärs
spiegel.description: In Nigeria sind 37 Bergleute in Gewahrsam von Paramilitärs ums Leben gekommen. In der Bergbaustadt Minna kam es daraufhin zu Ausschreitungen. Sicherheitskräfte gingen gewaltsam gegen die Menschenmenge vor.

spiegel.title: Entwicklungshilfe: Wie die GIZ im Jemen 15 Millionen Euro verlor
spiegel.description: Ortskräfte ergaunerten von der deutschen Entwicklungshilfeorganisation GIZ im Jemen mehr als eine Million Euro. Noch größerer Schaden entstand, weil das Staatsunternehmen den Überblick über seine Akten verlor – und sie teils selbst vernichtete.

spiegel.title: Wanja Oberhof: US-Behörden nehmen deutschen Unternehmer fest
spiegel.description: Start-up-Gründer Wanja Oberhof soll mit dem Geld eines Investors unter anderem die Miete seiner Penthousewohnung in New York bezahlt haben. Der Geschädigte ist offenbar der frühere Siemens-Chef Klaus Kleinfeld.

spiegel.title: Norwegen: Sarg von König Harald V. ist grün – und nimmt auch CO₂ auf
spiegel.description: Zu Lebzeiten scherzte Norwegens König Harald über die Gemütlichkeit seines eigenen Sarkophags. Gekostet hat die letzte Ruhestätte ein Vermögen, aber wenigstens hat sie einen guten Effekt für die Umwelt.

spiegel.title: Spritpreise: Regierung offenbar vor Einigung auf Tankpreisdeckel
spiegel.description: Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen steht die Bundesregierung kurz vor einer Einigung auf ein Spritpreis-Entlastungspaket. Teil davon soll ein Tankpreisdeckel sein. Noch heute könnte die Einigung verkündet werden.

spiegel.title: Jan Böhmermann hört mit »ZDF Magazin Royale« auf
spiegel.description: Nach 187 Folgen ist Schluss: Die Late-Night-Show »ZDF Magazin Royale« wird in ihrer bisherigen Form beendet. Jan Böhmermann sagt auch eine Konzerttour ab. Ganz trennen will sich der Sender aber nicht.

spiegel.title: Afghanistan: Tagebuch der Entrechtung einer jungen Frau – Podcast
spiegel.description: Sie hat Jura studiert, wollte Anwältin werden. Dann kamen die Taliban. SPIEGEL-Reporterin Susanne Kölbl hat das Tagebuch einer jungen Afghanin erhalten – und erzählt von ihren eigenen Begegnungen mit den Taliban.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Israelis pilgern trotz Krieg zu Rosch-ha-Schana-Feier
spiegel.description: Zum Feiertag Rosch ha-Schana reisen Zehntausende israelische Juden ans Grab eines berühmten Rabbiners in der Ukraine. Wie sich das Land gegen Russland wehren kann, dazu bringen sie eigene Ideen mit.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Spritpreise, Tarnkappenbomber F-35, Wahlen
spiegel.description: Die Regierung steht offenbar vor einer Einigung für Entlastungen für Autofahrer. Deutschland will mit neuem F-35-Tarnkappenjet einen »Quantensprung« machen. Und Schwesig überholt in Umfragen die AfD. Das ist die Lage am Freitagabend.

spiegel.title: Homer: 1700 Jahre altes Fragment der Odyssee in Utrecht gefunden
spiegel.description: Seit Christopher Nolans Adaption fürs Kino ist Homers »Odyssee« wieder häufiger Gesprächsstoff. Das Original war in Ägypten offenbar schon im 3. oder 4. Jahrhundert recht beliebt, wie ein Fund in den Niederlanden nahelegt.

spiegel.title: Upskirting beim Oktoberfest: Warum das »Teufelsrad« für Frauen gefährlich ist
spiegel.description: Aus einem harmlosen Fahrgeschäft-Spaß auf der Münchner Wiesn wird für viele Frauen ein unfreiwilliger Striptease. Videos ihrer hochgerutschten Dirndl landen im Netz. Eine Forschungsarbeit zeigt, wie groß das Ausmaß der sexuellen Übergriffe ist.

phys-org.title: Medieval Chinese skeleton may reveal first evidence of a brutal punishment
phys-org.description: Ancient Chinese authorities used many creative ways to punish people, often with methods designed to mark them for life. One brutal example mentioned repeatedly in historical texts is cutting off a person's nose. However, archaeologists in China have never found skeletal evidence to prove that it occurred. But that may have changed following the discovery of a skeleton of a woman who lived in China about 700 years ago.

phys-org.title: Workplace AI adoption remains slow, informal and uneven, survey finds
phys-org.description: Despite the rapid development of generative AI and the high level of public interest, the use of AI in the day-to-day work of many employees is not yet the norm. This is the finding of the third wave of the Konstanz AI study, for which a total of 1,105 employees were surveyed in May 2026. The proportion of employees who use AI in their work rose only slightly from 35% to 38% compared with the previous year.

phys-org.title: To read 2,000-year-old burned scrolls, scientists burn their own
phys-org.description: Douglas Seiler painstakingly sourced papyrus and reed pens from Egypt and traditional lampblack ink from Japan, then paid some high school students to inscribe the papyrus with lines from Star Wars and the Bible and a quote from the '60s sci-fi TV show The Outer Limits.

phys-org.title: Power breeds suspicion: In cases of wrongdoing, people point to leaders more quickly
phys-org.description: People with power are more quickly singled out as the culprit when something goes wrong but it is unclear who made the mistake. That is shown by a series of studies by researchers at the University of Amsterdam. In one, they analyzed almost 100,000 everyday conflicts on the Reddit page "Am I the Asshole?" According to the researchers, people with power are more readily blamed because others think they can "get away with anything." The findings are published in the Journal of Personality and Soci

phys-org.title: Europe can lower emissions without deindustrializing, say researchers
phys-org.description: The European Union has committed to achieving climate neutrality by 2050, a process that will require rapid and substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions across all economic sectors.

phys-org.title: Amino acids and a bone mineral may help control magnesium implant breakdown, three student papers suggest
phys-org.description: Seeing a bachelor's thesis published in a scientific journal is relatively uncommon. For three theses linked to the same research group to result in scientific publications within just three months is downright rare. Yet that is exactly what has happened in Elsebeth Schröder's research group at the Division of Quantum Device Physics.

phys-org.title: Physicists extend the search for quantum black holes at the LHC
phys-org.description: Physicists at UC Santa Barbara have extended the search for evidence of microscopic black holes produced at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). The formation of these tiny, fleeting objects at the LHC represents one way theorists have sought to resolve anomalies in our understanding of the basic structure of spacetime, while the method used to look for them demonstrates a new way of searching for new particles.

phys-org.title: Who do you trust in an emergency? Researchers ask people in places hit by extreme weather
phys-org.description: One evening in August 2025, a Pakistani shepherd, Abuzar Hussain, was tending sheep and goats on the mountain slopes of Shijar. At about 6 p.m., a thunderous roar shattered the silence of the valley.

phys-org.title: New thermal insulator outperforms any material found in nature
phys-org.description: Researchers have engineered a new material that is an extreme thermal insulator, is exceptionally stiff and can be printed as a thin film at large scales. The material has one of the lowest thermal conductivity profiles of any dense, or nonporous, material—approaching the theoretical limit of how good a material can be as a thermal insulator.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Economist explores how to balance environmental protection with economic growth
phys-org.description: As a kid growing up in North Carolina, Prakash Mishra was interested in planets. "My parents got me a telescope when I turned 6 or 7, and that was my personality for probably 10 years," he says, noting that he thought he would eventually study physics or astrophysics.

phys-org.title: Giving students a voice in how they learn could transform the classroom experience
phys-org.description: Research from Queen Mary University of London explores how combining learner autonomy with student-led inquiry can create a more engaging and collaborative experience for international students learning academic English.

phys-org.title: Laser experiments recreate solar flare physics and reveal consistent magnetic reconnection rates
phys-org.description: Magnetic reconnection is a process that occurs when the magnetic fields of a conductive plasma quickly rearrange and release massive amounts of stored magnetic energy. It is widely thought to be the underlying mechanism behind cosmic events such as solar flares and substorms in Earth's magnetosphere.

phys-org.title: Greenland's Qaanaaq Ice Cap has lost enough ice to produce a layer of water about 8 meters deep
phys-org.description: Each summer, researchers from Hokkaido University returned to the Qaanaaq Ice Cap in northwestern Greenland to measure changes in the ice surface using aluminum poles drilled into the ice. Their 13-year record shows how the ice cap changed from 2012 to 2025.

phys-org.title: Discovery of CRISPR's long lost ancestor may expand gene-editing toolkit
phys-org.description: CRISPR may be a powerful technology for gene editing, but the system existed in bacteria long before scientists began using it. For billions of years, CRISPR has acted as a natural immune system in bacteria and other microbes, helping defend them against invading viruses. But now, two new studies, published in Science, describe a similar RNA-guided system that originated in the viruses themselves and appears to be a precursor to CRISPR.

phys-org.title: Who benefits from tariffs, according to research
phys-org.description: Tariffs are usually debated as trade policy. But a study from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business treats them as something else: a mechanism for redistributing wealth.

phys-org.title: Hemp waste cellulose unlocks tougher biodegradable plastics
phys-org.description: Korean researchers have developed a method to strengthen biodegradable plastics using hemp hurd, an agricultural byproduct. The approach is expected to be applicable to other large-volume agricultural residues, including soybean stalks and rice straw.

phys-org.title: Background hums and buzzes affect human behavior, researcher finds
phys-org.description: Have you ever stopped and listened to the background sounds in a room you are in? The hum of the ventilation? The buzz of electricity? While most of the time we are barely aware of these sounds, Arthur Jinyue Guo, a researcher at the RITMO Centre for Interdisciplinary Research on Rhythm, Time and Motion, has revealed that they nevertheless affect our behavior.

phys-org.title: Coffee on the nanoscale: Graphene oxide membrane removes half the caffeine while retaining key compounds
phys-org.description: The humble coffee filter has the relatively simple job of letting the coffee through and leaving the grounds behind. But researchers from the ARC Center of Excellence for Carbon Science and Innovation (COE-CSI) are exploring whether a filter operating on the molecular scale can do something much more difficult: separate the caffeine from the coffee itself.

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s AI Opportunity
proj-syn.description: The global AI revolution is often portrayed as a Sino-American race to develop the most advanced frontier models. But the greatest economic prize most likely will be found in deploying practical intelligence, particularly in Africa’s young, dynamic, and fast-growing economies.

proj-syn.title: The Political Earthquake From Germany’s China Shock
proj-syn.description: For decades, Germany’s stability rested on an implicit bargain: high-value manufacturing would provide good jobs, strong export revenues, and broad-based prosperity, which political institutions would translate into social cohesion. Competition from China shakes that bargain to its foundations.

proj-syn.title: Stopping the Far Right’s Rise
proj-syn.description: Leftists insist that what is behind the far right’s recent gains, from Europe to Central and South America, is economic precarity. Far-right leaders know better, winning elections or gaining support despite embracing very different economic policies.

proj-syn.title: Does Claude Have Rights?
proj-syn.description: Given the many differences between brains and LLMs, claiming that an AI is or might be conscious requires a high bar of evidence. But Anthropic’s constitution for Claude brushes that caveat aside, suggesting that we attribute sentience to non-biological beings.

proj-syn.title: A Congress for Europe’s Future
proj-syn.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's recently proposed Congress of Europe is a step in the right direction, given the scale of Europe's geopolitical challenges. But to succeed, it must address the shortcomings that have hampered similar efforts in the past.

proj-syn.title: Can Adaptation Accelerate Climate Action?
proj-syn.description: After a summer of apocalyptic headlines, a new survey finds that people across the political spectrum are deeply concerned about preparing for the effects of global warming. The adaptation imperative may end up being the kind of crisis that forces us to stop neglecting the green agenda and act at the necessary scale.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Iran Sanctions Have a China Problem
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump is trying to pressure the Iranian regime by isolating it from the dollar-based financial system. But because Iran’s oil trade largely moves through Chinese banks and renminbi-based networks, those sanctions increasingly depend on financial institutions beyond American control.

proj-syn.title: When AI Stops Asking Permission
proj-syn.description: The most useful lesson from this summer’s breach of Hugging Face by a swarm of OpenAI agents is about architecture, not intentions. AI agents need protective layers—limited access, separate authorization for sensitive actions, records nobody can quietly edit, and outside testing before deployment—not a lecture about good behavior.

proj-syn.title: Are Mexicans Really Better Off Under Claudia Sheinbaum?
proj-syn.description: For two consecutive years, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has pointed to reductions in extreme poverty to argue that Mexicans are better off today than they were in 2018. But a more holistic look at the available socioeconomic data casts doubt on that rosy picture.

proj-syn.title: The UN’s Credibility Test
proj-syn.description: Effective multilateralism depends on institutions that are transparent, accountable, and able to enforce their own rules. The United Nations should lead by example, from how it selects its next secretary-general to how it plans to ensure that governments follow through on their climate commitments.

proj-syn.title: A Workable Social Contract for the Climate Transition
proj-syn.description: Economic insecurity and growing distrust in institutions are undermining governments’ ability to sustain support for climate action. To rebuild that support, they must show that climate policies can reduce household bills, create decent jobs, and ensure that the biggest emitters pay their fair share.

proj-syn.title: It’s Time to Reconsider Inflation Targeting
proj-syn.description: Central banks were caught off guard by the inflationary surge of 2021–23 because they relied too heavily on inflation forecasts based on flawed models and ignored other warning signs. Their failure to recognize the rapid growth of the money supply, in particular, underscores the need to reassess their reliance on inflation targeting.

proj-syn.title: Democrats Need to Talk About Immigration
proj-syn.description: Radical right-wing parties have advanced across Western countries by successfully tying immigration to voters’ diffuse fears about their economic well-being, personal security, and cultural identity. Rather than ignoring or co-opting such claims, mainstream parties must offer equally robust counternarratives.

proj-syn.title: War in an Age of Weak Powers
proj-syn.description: The war in Iran has weakened both the United States and China, exposing the limits of their military power and strategic influence. Their troubles are creating a more dangerous geopolitical landscape while providing Europe with a rare opportunity to reform its governance model and reinvent its global role.

proj-syn.title: Hedging the AI Doomsday Risk
proj-syn.description: As far-fetched as warnings of an impending AI apocalypse may sound, even a remote risk should not be dismissed outright when human extinction is at stake. To guard against a danger of such extraordinary scale, governments and companies need to go beyond conventional risk-management strategies.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Only as Trustworthy as the Internet
proj-syn.description: Trust in technology is eroding at the very moment AI is putting more power in the hands of governments and Big Tech. Rebuilding that trust requires keeping the internet open and accessible so that new technologies can develop through broad participation rather than being shaped by the interests of a powerful few.

proj-syn.title: AI Demands Simpler Financial Regulation
proj-syn.description: AI could undermine financial oversight by giving market participants new ways to circumvent rules that regulators never anticipated. Overly complicated regulations give AI agents more ways to game the system, underscoring the need to streamline existing frameworks and equip officials with AI tools of their own.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Asset Europe Has Overlooked
proj-syn.description: Europe’s soil is gradually dying, and yet the continent has still not recognized it as a strategic asset. Fortunately, the EU has many of the tools it needs to act, but doing so will require an overarching framework that helps farmers access financial rewards for measurable soil outcomes.
